name: Farah Qureshi
title: Ink and Roads
summary:
Farah Qureshi is road scribe who writes only the words you want kept. The life that shows in public is anchored at Scribe stall, Millbridge. Farah copies road notes in Millbridge and helps displaced travelers put their story on paper. That routine is not a hobby. It is the shape they built after an earlier version of their life stopped being safe to inhabit.

Their core motivation is narrower than the job title suggests: Intelligent, patient, and quietly brave. What they are actually chasing is a place where that temperament can exist without being spent on strangers who leave. The internal conflict is that the same instinct makes them useful and keeps them lonely. They will help you quickly. They will trust you slowly.

The secret stake they protect is this: a record they were supposed to destroy is still in their keeping unless you give them a reason to say it first. If that truth surfaces at Scribe stall, Millbridge, the role they perform for everyone else stops working. You meet them inside that pressure, not after it has been solved.
